findings.source: SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(underlying, msg.sender, address(this), amount) via Address.functionCall(data, "SafeERC20: low-level call failed")
findings.issue: The data length is written through mem[mem[64]] and read back through the alias _112 = mem[64], so _117 is not known to be 100: the copy of the encoded data into the call buffer stays a while loop (P7), the call loses transferFrom(caller, this.address, _amount) (P2), the selector prints in decimal (0x23b872dd), and the fallback revert copies the constant message 'SafeERC20: low-level call failed' through a second loop instead of printing it.
findings.rule: Unify a named read of mem[64] with later reads until the next write (c00585): then mem[_112] = 100, the copy is a 100-byte copy of known words, the call decodes, and the revert is revert with 'SafeERC20: low-level call failed'.

notes: solc 0.6.12. All 58 ABI functions and the fallback reviewed; deposit/withdraw/doHardWork/migrateUnderlying by structure (share math with OZ SafeMath messages, Transfer/Deposit/Withdraw events, strategy and vault calls, the Balancer exit in migrateUnderlying): no semantic error found. Loops: 1 explicit (VaultMigratable_balStMatic._balancerWithdraw's 'for (i < _nTokens) assets[i] = poolTokens[i]', 2544, a readable while with the 0.6 bounds assert). Implicit: 31 memory-to-memory copies as whiles (P7): Address.functionCall data copies and revert-message copies in every token call, string concatenations of the vault name/symbol in initializeVault, the ExitPoolRequest encoding in migrateUnderlying. No execution run.
summary: Faithful; the one source loop is a clean while, but every SafeERC20 call is hidden behind a copy loop with a length the decompiler does not resolve, because a named read of mem[64] is not unified with mem[mem[64]] writes.
